The pricing manager indicates that each zone holds an ad
week. Additionally, some ad weeks may be big sales, e.g.,
during holidays.
The marketing director comments that, during big sale events,
more shoppers go through the doors.
At the moment, we do not believe the input from the IT
personnel provides valuable information to determine the
cause of empty shelves and margin collapse.
The store operations show that restocking is done on a fixed
schedule. Fixed delivery schedules after a big sale may cause
empty shelves.
The distribution center manager mentions that, during sales,
advertised products are prioritized for delivery.
The finance team indicates that margains depend on unit cost
(which is reduced during sales) and the number of items sold.
Thus, if a large number of customers buy only from the
advertised products, it may lead to decreased margains.
The store manager wants to remove sales to avoid margain
collapse, implying that big sale events are directly related to
empty shelves and margain collapse.
